Senses.Explanation: The wooden buddha is a materially wooden image in Danxia Tianran’s burning case and in the fixed contrast that a wooden buddha does not pass through fire. Literally a "buddha" (佛) made of "wood" (木): a "wooden buddha," attested 663 times in 181 allowlisted texts. The principal recorded case says Danxia, encountering severe cold at Huilin Temple, took a wooden buddha and burned it. When the superintendent rebuked him, Danxia stirred the ashes and said he was looking for relics. The superintendent replied, "How could a wooden buddha have relics?" Danxia said, "Since it has no relics, bring two more honored ones to burn" (木佛何有舍利，既無舍利，更請兩尊來燒). The phrase also appears in the fixed line "a wooden buddha does not pass through fire" (木佛不度火), alongside a clay buddha not passing through water and a gold buddha not passing through a furnace.
Senses.Note: Later masters repeatedly raise the Danxia case and ask why the superintendent's eyebrows fell out. Recorded answers include "a thief does not raid a poor household" (賊不打貧兒家), "one person transmits a falsehood; ten thousand transmit it as fact" (一人傳虗，萬人傳實), "Zhang drinks the wine and Li gets drunk," and "the cat knows how to climb a tree." The ten occurrences of "What is a wooden buddha?" (the question “What is a wooden Buddha?”) and these later questions retain the literal image as their headword; the texts do not replace it with an abstract category.
